title: AWS CDK
description: Define AWS infrastructure using the AWS Cloud Development Kit (CDK) with constructs, stacks, and apps in familiar programming languages.

data.text: The AWS Cloud Development Kit (CDK) lets you define cloud infrastructure using familiar programming languages like TypeScript, Python, Java, and C#. Instead of writing raw JSON/YAML CloudFormation templates, you use CDK constructs that represent AWS resources as objects.

The CDK has three main concepts: constructs (the building blocks that represent AWS resources), stacks (collections of constructs that deploy together), and apps (the container for your stacks). When you run `cdk deploy`, the CDK synthesizes your code into a CloudFormation template and deploys it.

data.title: CDK Core Concepts
items: **Construct** — an AWS resource represented as a class (e.g., s3.Bucket, lambda.Function)
**Stack** — a unit of deployment containing related constructs
**App** — the top-level container that holds one or more stacks
**CDK Toolkit** — the CLI that synthesizes and deploys stacks

data.text: CDK constructs are the building blocks. Level 1 (L1) constructs map directly to CloudFormation resources. Level 2 (L2) constructs provide higher-level abstractions with sensible defaults. Level 3 (L3) constructs are patterns like AWS CDK Pipelines.

When you deploy, the CDK synthesizes your stacks into CloudFormation templates, uploads assets to S3, and creates or updates CloudFormation stacks. The CDK also handles rollback if something goes wrong.

data.content: A CDK stack that creates an S3 bucket and a Lambda function.

terms.definition: A basic building block in CDK that represents a cloud component such as an S3 bucket or Lambda function.
A CDK unit of deployment that translates to a CloudFormation stack.
The process of converting CDK code into a CloudFormation template before deployment.
The top-level CDK construct that contains one or more stacks.

data.title: Build a CDK Stack
data.description: Create a CDK app in TypeScript that provisions an S3 bucket, a Lambda function, and an API Gateway.
steps: Initialize a new CDK project with `cdk init app --language typescript`
Add an S3 bucket construct with versioning and encryption
Add a Lambda function construct with an S3 bucket name environment variable
Grant the Lambda function read access to the bucket
Synthesize the stack and inspect the CloudFormation template
data.expectedOutcome: You will see a CloudFormation template generated from your CDK code with the S3 bucket and Lambda function defined.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: CDK lets you define infrastructure using programming languages instead of JSON/YAML
Constructs represent AWS resources as objects with methods and properties
Stacks are deployed as CloudFormation stacks
CDK combines the power of code with the reliability of CloudFormation
data.takeaway: CDK is the preferred way to write infrastructure as code on AWS. It is more expressive and maintainable than raw CloudFormation.
